sourceObservations.observation: The source relates flux through a loop of area S to the cosine of the angle between its normal and the magnetic induction vector: Phi=BS cos(alpha). It uses the normal, not the plane of the loop, to define that angle.

The source says alpha increases proportionally to time under uniform angular rotation and gives alpha=omega t. This is an accumulated rotation phase, not an indefinitely increasing geometric principal angle between two vectors.

The resulting Phi=BS cos(omega t) requires the normal to sweep in a plane containing B, with phase zero chosen at normal/B alignment. Uniform rotation without that orientation condition would not alone imply the stated full-amplitude cosine.

independentSourceAssessment.sourceShorthand: The local source is physically coherent as the usual ideal rotating-loop model, but its angle terminology is shorthand: a geometric principal angle folds back after a half-turn, whereas an accumulated rotation phase continues to increase.
necessaryAffectedExplanation: State the normal's rotation plane contains B, and choose time zero when the normal is aligned with B.
Identify alpha=omega t as accumulated rotation phase that may exceed a half-turn or a full turn.
Distinguish the instantaneous geometric principal angle to B, which is bounded by a half-turn and does not increase indefinitely.
Explain that phase and principal angle have the same cosine, so the original flux formula and the following time-dependent flux expression remain equivalent.
Retain all original formulas and notation; clarification of the prose does not authorize a mathematical substitution.
independentSourceAssessment.languageCriteria: Both Chinese and English must present the same conditions, distinguish phase from principal angle explicitly, and connect cosine equivalence to flux in a complete, natural explanatory sequence.
